name: Master of Engineering (Civil Infrastructure)
description: This two-year course takes graduates of related degrees into the design of bridges, roads and drainage networks. Students work through design studios and site-based case studies. A supervised project in the second year ties the units together.

name: Master of Engineering Management
description: A one-year course for engineers who are moving into supervisory roles. It covers planning, budgeting, contracts and safety management through case discussions and group assignments. Graduates learn to run a technical team as well as a technical task.

name: Master of Robotics and Intelligent Systems
description: Students build and program robots across two years, starting with kinematics and control and moving to vision and planning. Most units run as lab sessions where code is tested on real hardware. The final year is a capstone in which a team delivers a working machine.

name: Diploma of Engineering Technology (Mechanical)
description: A two-year diploma that teaches the drawing, workshop and calculation skills used in mechanical engineering support work. Classes mix computer-aided drawing with hands-on machining. It can lead on to degree study.

name: Master of Renewable Energy Engineering
description: This course covers how solar, wind and battery systems are designed and connected to the electricity grid. Students model systems in software and test components in the power laboratory. Over two years the focus moves from single installations to whole networks.

name: Diploma of Biomedical Engineering Technology
description: A one-year diploma for people who want to maintain and test the equipment used in clinics and hospitals. Students learn basic anatomy and electronics, then practise calibrating and safety-checking devices. Work placements give time in a real equipment workshop.

name: Master of Engineering (Electrical Power Systems)
description: Aimed at electrical graduates who want to work on generation, transmission and distribution. The units teach fault analysis, protection schemes and system control, mostly through simulation exercises. Students finish with an applied project in the second year.

name: Master of Engineering (Mechanical)
description: A two-year coursework degree for graduates who want to design machines and thermal systems. It teaches modelling, analysis and testing, with a good deal of time in design studios. Industry-set problems feature in the project units.

name: Master of Project Management (Engineering and Construction)
description: Students learn how large engineering and construction projects are planned, priced and controlled. Teaching is built around scheduling tools, contract documents and real project case studies. It suits engineers and technical staff who already have some site experience.

name: Master of Biomedical Engineering
description: This course brings engineering methods to problems in medicine, such as joint replacement, imaging and monitoring devices. Students study physiology alongside mechanics and electronics, then design a device in a team project. Clinical placements are available in the second year.

name: Diploma of Engineering Studies
description: A one-year bridging diploma that prepares students for an engineering degree. It revises mathematics and physics and introduces design thinking and basic programming. Small classes and regular problem sessions keep the pace manageable.

name: Master of Solar and Wind Energy Systems
description: Over one year, students learn to assess a site, size a solar or wind installation and model its output. The course is taught through design exercises and software modelling rather than long lectures. It finishes with a feasibility study of a full project.

name: Master of Mechatronic Engineering
description: Mechatronics joins mechanical design, electronics and software, and this course teaches all three over two years. Students build small automated systems from the first semester. Later units cover industrial controllers and a team project with a working prototype.

name: Master of Engineering (Structural)
description: This course is for graduates who want to specialise in how buildings and bridges carry load. Students design in steel and concrete, check designs with modelling software and learn the relevant codes. A major design project closes the second year.

name: Diploma of Civil Construction Design
description: A practical one-year diploma in preparing the drawings and documents that civil construction crews work from. Students draft roads, drains and earthworks plans on computer and practise reading site surveys. Placements put the skills to use on live projects.

name: Diploma of Electrical Engineering
description: This two-year diploma teaches the theory behind electrical systems and how to apply it to installations and controllers. About half the time is spent in workshops wiring, testing and programming equipment. Students graduate able to work as technicians or continue to a degree.

name: Diploma of Mechanical Engineering Technology
description: Students learn to draw, make and maintain mechanical parts and assemblies. The course alternates between design software and workshop practice on lathes, mills and test rigs. It is a hands-on route for people who prefer learning by doing.

name: Diploma of Renewable Energy Technology
description: A one-year diploma on installing and servicing solar and battery systems. Students size arrays, wire small systems and test them on the training roof. Safety on site is taught in every unit.

name: Diploma of Robotics and Automation Technology
description: This course teaches the basics of programming and servicing automated machines and small robot arms. Students wire controllers, write simple programs and troubleshoot faults in the lab. It is a short, practical start for a career in automation.

name: Diploma of Engineering Project Support
description: A one-year diploma for people who help engineering projects run smoothly behind the scenes. It covers record keeping, schedules, ordering and cost tracking using common software. Placement time lets students practise on real project teams.

name: Diploma of Biomedical Equipment Servicing
description: Students learn to service, test and repair the machines used in healthcare, from patient monitors to sterilisers. The course combines electronics theory with bench work on donated equipment. Careful record keeping and safety checking are part of every unit.

name: Master of Engineering (Civil and Environmental)
description: This course joins civil design with the care of land and water. Students study how rivers, drains and treatment plants behave and how projects are assessed for their effects on the environment. The second year is given over to a research or design project.

name: Master of Electrical Engineering
description: A two-year course covering power, electronics and control for electrical graduates. Lectures are paired with laboratory work and design studios. Students can lean towards energy or towards electronics in the second year.

name: Master of Engineering Project Management
description: This one-year course teaches engineers to plan and deliver projects on time and within budget. Case studies and group simulations make up most of the assessment. It suits working engineers who want formal management training.

name: Diploma of Engineering Foundations
description: A diploma that builds the mathematics, physics and drawing skills needed to start an engineering degree. Classes are small and include regular tutoring. Students who pass can move straight into the first year of a degree.

name: Master of Renewable Energy and Power Systems
description: Students learn how renewable generation is built into working power systems, including microgrids and storage. Teaching mixes modelling exercises with laboratory demonstrations. A short placement or industry project fills the final term.

name: Master of Biomedical Engineering Practice
description: The course trains engineers to work alongside clinicians on devices that measure or assist the body. Students learn signal processing and instrumentation, then design and test a device in the project units. Hospital-based placements form part of the second year.

name: Master of Engineering (Civil)
description: A two-year degree for graduates who want to design and build urban infrastructure. Studio classes use building information modelling and real design briefs. The capstone asks students to produce a complete civil design package.

name: Master of Mechatronics and Robotics Engineering
description: This course teaches how to design robots from the sensors and motors through to the software that drives them. Students spend much of their time in the robotics lab. The two years end with a capstone in which teams build and demonstrate a robotic system.

name: Master of Engineering Management
description: Built for engineers who are ready to lead people and budgets as well as designs. It covers project control, finance and operations through workshops and case analyses. The course runs for one year.

name: Master of Biomedical Engineering
description: Students apply engineering to the body, studying imaging, instruments, implants and tissue repair. Laboratory classes run alongside design projects set by clinical partners. A capstone project completes the two years.

name: Diploma of Engineering Practice
description: A two-year diploma that gives a broad base in engineering before choosing a specialty. Students try small design tasks in civil, mechanical and electrical work. Strong results can count towards a full engineering degree.

name: Master of Engineering (Electrical Power)
description: This course covers how electricity is generated, moved and controlled. Students analyse networks, design converters and study how energy markets shape operation. The second year has a major project built on a real network problem.

name: Master of Sustainable Energy Engineering
description: A one-year course on designing energy systems that cut waste and use clean sources. Students model buildings, solar farms and storage, and assess them across their whole life. The final project tackles a real design or planning question.

name: Master of Engineering (Mechanical)
description: Over two years, students develop deep skills in analysing and designing mechanical systems. Computer simulation sits beside laboratory testing in most units. The research project lets students investigate one question in detail.

name: Master of Chemical and Process Engineering
description: This course teaches how chemicals and materials are made at scale. Students design plants, model reactions and study safety and control. Plant design work in the second year draws everything together.

name: Master of Autonomous Systems Engineering
description: The course covers machines that sense their surroundings and decide how to move, such as drones and ground vehicles. Students write navigation and control software and test it in simulation and on small vehicles. A two-year project closes the course.

name: Master of Energy Systems Engineering
description: Students study how clean energy sources are generated, stored and delivered through electricity networks. Modelling and laboratory work run side by side. The second year includes an extended project on a real energy problem.

name: Master of Biomedical Engineering and Devices
description: This course teaches how to design, test and bring to clinic the devices used in diagnosis and treatment. Students move between engineering labs and clinical settings. A research project in the second year goes into one problem in depth.

name: Diploma of Engineering Foundations
description: A one-year pathway course for students who need extra preparation before entering an engineering degree. It teaches mathematics, physics and design in small groups. Teachers set regular problem work and give prompt feedback.

name: Master of Engineering Project Management
description: A one-year course on planning, running and closing out engineering projects. Students use industry scheduling tools and work through contract and risk cases. It is suited to engineers moving into coordinator or manager roles.

name: Master of Engineering (Structures and Geotechnics)
description: This course looks at how structures and the ground beneath them work together. Students design foundations, frames and retaining walls and check their results by modelling. Placement time on civil projects is available.

name: Master of Electrical and Electronic Engineering
description: Students build knowledge of circuits, communications and power over two years. Laboratory sessions let them design and test hardware, while project units tackle larger systems. The course suits graduates from science or related engineering degrees.

name: Master of Robotics and Mechatronics Engineering
description: This course covers the design of robots and mechatronic machines, from arms on a factory floor to small mobile robots. Students program, build and test in the lab throughout. The project units invite teams to solve a problem set by an outside client.

name: Master of Engineering Project Management
description: A one-year course that treats project management as an engineering skill. Students plan projects, track cost and manage risk through realistic simulations. A short placement or project report rounds out the year.

name: Diploma of Engineering Technology
description: A two-year diploma that blends theory with workshop practice across mechanical and electrical subjects. Students draw, build and test small assemblies. Placement experience is built into the second year.

name: Master of Solar Energy Engineering
description: This one-year course looks closely at solar power, from how a cell turns light into current to how a farm is designed. Lab work tests real panels and inverters. Students end the year with a design project.

name: Master of Medical Device Engineering
description: Students learn how a medical device moves from idea to safe, tested product. The units cover materials, electronics, quality systems and clinical testing. Teams design a device prototype during the year, with input from clinicians.

name: Master of Engineering (Mechanical)
description: A two-year degree in analysing and designing mechanical systems, with a lean towards manufacturing. Students use simulation software and practise on workshop equipment. The final project is a design carried from concept to prototype.

name: Master of Engineering (Civil)
description: The course covers structures, water and transport for graduates who want to practise civil engineering. Students work on design problems drawn from real sites. Two years of study finish with a substantial project.

name: Master of Electrical Engineering
description: This course teaches electrical engineering to graduates from related fields. Students begin with circuits and signals, then move on to power and control. Project work gives time to design, build and test a working system.

name: Diploma of Engineering Technology (Civil)
description: A one-year diploma in the skills a civil technician uses every day: surveying, drafting and understanding construction materials. Practical sessions are held outdoors on the campus grounds. Placements are arranged on local civil projects.

name: Master of Renewable Energy Engineering
description: This one-year course teaches students to design wind and solar projects and to connect them to the grid. Teaching includes modelling tasks and a feasibility study. It builds on a first degree in engineering or science.

name: Master of Engineering Management
description: Designed for engineers moving into leadership, this course covers budgeting, risk and the management of technical staff. Students work through case studies drawn from engineering projects. It runs for one year.

name: Master of Engineering (Civil and Hydraulic)
description: A two-year course in structures and water engineering, with attention to rivers, dams and coasts. Students use hydraulic models and field data in class. Field trips and a design project give practice on real sites.

name: Master of Engineering (Electrical and Power)
description: This course trains graduates to work on electrical generation and supply. Students analyse power networks, design controls and study how new sources connect to the grid. The second year centres on an applied project.

name: Master of Engineering (Mechanical and Marine)
description: A two-year course for graduates who want to design vessels and the machinery that drives them. It covers hull forms, propulsion and structures, using computer models and tank testing. A major design project is completed in the second year.

name: Master of Renewable Energy Engineering
description: This course looks at hydro, wind and storage and how they make up a clean energy supply. Students model plants, study the electrical side and consider how projects are financed. The second year is a project on a real or realistic site.

name: Diploma of Engineering Practice
description: A one-year diploma that gives an all-round start in engineering. It covers calculation, drawing and basic computing, with workshop sessions to make ideas concrete. Students can carry credit into a degree.

name: Master of Engineering Project Management
description: A one-year course on running engineering projects, from first plan to handover. Students practise scheduling, costing and risk analysis in group exercises. The course suits engineers already working in the field.

name: Master of Robotics for Marine and Field Systems
description: This one-year course is about robots that work outdoors and on the water. Students study sensing, navigation and control, then test small vehicles in field exercises. A project closes the year with a robot built to meet a stated task.
